inspiration: One shape, many metals: each metal item points at a shared texture plus a palette PNG (copper_ingot.zig.zon line 4; the loader is src/items.zig line 42, loadColorsFromTexture). Gold, copper, iron and silver differ by palette and roughness, not by a separate sprite. For gold-plated armour: one plate shape, a gilt palette ramp with a few dark seams, and a low roughness so the highlight is sharp. Keep the palette swap; change the ramp hues and the seam pattern.

Material as a small stat block: gold has durability 400, massDamage 14.0, swingSpeed 0.25 and textureRoughness 0.05 (gold_ingot.zig.zon lines 2-10); copper has durability 300 and roughness 0.1. Tags (.metal, .precious) sit beside the stats. Idea: a loot rarity or metal class as tags plus a few numbers, not a new item type.

Roughness defaults to a high value: src/items.zig line 78 sets textureRoughness to the file value, floored at 0, and uses 1.0 when the field is missing. Idea for our shaders: a safe default for any material with no finish value.

Tools from a part grid: sword.zig.zon has a 5 x 5 disabled grid and a 5 x 5 optional grid (lines 3-16) and a parameter matrix that maps a material stat to a tool stat. A crafted weapon is a mask of parts, and the stats come from the parts. Idea for crafted or procedural weapons, kept out of the fight loop.

A rare set piece with a very low chance: meteorite.zig.zon sets chance 0.00002 (line 4) and one structure with a placement mode of all. The structure refers to cubyz:meteorite/base; the matching .blp was not listed (folder assets/cubyz/sbb/meteorite/ exists). Idea for row 23 zone population and loot: rare set pieces as data with a chance, not a hand-placed spawn.

Small creature data: snail.zig.zon is four fields (model id, default texture, height 1, right-handed y-up). The creature look is a model plus a texture id; the behaviour lives elsewhere. Idea for row 7 (creature actor): keep creature data this small and point at a model.

Layered biome and cave data: the cave_layers folder has at least five layer files (sky, surface caves, void root transition, void, caves) and the biomes folder has 35 entries. Idea for zone-as-data: each zone is a stack of layers with its own rules, not one big script.

Tool icons with a per-part overlay: tools/ holds a base 16 x 16 sprite and an overlay sprite per tool (sword, pickaxe, axe, chisel, sickle, shover). Idea for weapon variants readable at 375 px: a base silhouette plus a small coloured overlay for the head or the grip.

briefs.label: Gilt plate armour (own label)
briefs.why: One plate shape with a palette ramp and a low roughness reads as expensive metal without a second sprite.
briefs.keep: one shared greyscale plate texture; a palette ramp swap per metal; a low roughness so the highlight is sharp
briefs.change: plate silhouette (our own pauldron and skirt shapes); ramp hues (warm brass, not a plain gold); engraved seam pattern of our own
briefs.ref: assets/cubyz/items/gold_ingot.zig.zon lines 2 and 10; assets/cubyz/items/copper_ingot.zig.zon line 4; src/items.zig line 42

briefs.label: Part-grid hewing tool (own label)
briefs.why: A weapon built from a mask of parts gives many looks from few sprites and stats that follow the parts.
briefs.keep: a mask grid of present or absent parts; a matrix that maps one material stat to one tool stat; an overlay sprite per part
briefs.change: our part set (no sword, axe and pickaxe layout); our tag names; a grip-and-blade silhouette of our own

briefs.label: Meteor crater set piece (own label)
briefs.why: A very rare landmark with its own blueprint makes a walk worth doing and gives row 23 a rare-zone type.
briefs.keep: a chance near 1 in 50000 per cell; one placement mode; a blueprint file per family
briefs.change: our crater shape and palette; a fight arena in the centre rather than loot; our own trigger for the set piece
